annotations.title: He that ſhal ouercome.
annotations.text: In al theſe ſpeaches to diuers Biſhops and their Churches, <mn>◦</mn> he continually encourageth them to conſtancie in faith and good life, by ſetting before their eies the revvard of the next life. And yet the Caluiniſts would haue no man do good in reſpect of ſuch revvard.

notes.text: Doing wel in respect of reward.

annotations.title: Adore before thy feete.
annotations.text: ◦ You ſee this vvord of adoration is in Scriptures vſed for worſhip of creatures alſo, and that to fall before the feete of holy men or Angels for duety and reuerence, is not idolatrie, except the proper honour due to God, be giuen vnto them. See the Annotations vpon the 19 & 22 Chapter concerning the Apoſtles proſtration before the Angel. And the Aduerſaries euaſion, ſaying that the adoration was of God onely: and that, before the feete of the partie, ſignifieth nothing els but, in his preſence, is falſe and againſt the phraſe of Scriptures. as 4 Reg. 4. vvhere the Sunamite adored Eliſæus, falling downe before his feete, and 4 Reg. 2. the ſonnes of the Prophets adored him in the ſame ſort. and here this adoration can not be meant but of the Biſhop or Angel of Philadelphia, becauſe he promiſeth this honour as a revvard, and as an effecte of his loue towardes him, ſaying, And they ſhal know that I haue loued thee. And that vvhich he ſaith in the 22 Chapter, I fel downe to adore before the feete of the Angel: the very ſame he expreſſeth thus in the 19 Chapter, I fel before his feete to adore him: making it al one, to adore before his feete, and to adore him.

annotations.title: That no man take thy crowne.
annotations.text: That is, his crowne of euerlaſting life and glorie, if he perſeuere not to the end in faith & good vvorkes: <mn>◦</mn> otherwiſe an other ſhal enter into his place, as Mathias did both to the dignitie of the Apoſtleſhip, & to the heauenly crowne due for the wel vſing and executing of the ſame function: which Iudas might and ſhould haue had, if he had perſeuered to the end. and as the Gentiles came into the grace and place of the Iewes. Other difficulties concerning this kinde of ſpeache are reſolued in Schoolemen, and are not here to be ſtoode vpon.

notes.text: Perseuerance in good & continuing to the end.

annotations.title: Lukevvarme.
annotations.text: Zeale and feruour is commendable, ſpecially in Gods cauſe: <mn>◦</mn> and the Neuters that be neither hote nor cold, are to Chriſt and his Church burdenous and lothſome, as lukewarme water is to a mans ſtomake, prouoking him to vomite. and therfore he threateneth to void vp ſuch Neuters out of his mouth.
